v5.re: ^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} \| Synthetic entry [12] \| Synthetic entry [12] \| R [12]\.00 \| Delete$

entries.reason: The Amount is parsed as an amount in rand (integer cents: digits, an optional R, groups of three, '.' and at most 2 decimals; a credit may be negative) and anything else is refused with a message that keeps the typed text. v5 accepted any text and showed what fmtR made of it, so the sweep's synthetic text 'Synthetic entry N' was saved and shown as R N.00; in the app both synthetic entries are refused and the register stays empty (S-disbursements_tab-1, no validation).
entries.author: CC-07 worker (GRS-17)

entries.reason: After the two synthetic entries v5's table has 2 rows; the app refused both (IDR-282), so its table holds only the empty-state row (S-disbursements_tab-1).

v5.re: ^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} \| Synthetic entry [12] \| Synthetic entry [12] \| Synthetic entry [12] \| Synthetic entry [12] \| [^|]* \| R 0\.00 \| Delete$

entries.reason: Hours and Rate/h are parsed as numbers (hours in hundredths, the rate in integer cents, '.' decimals, no negative, bounded) and Value is computed exactly; anything else is refused with a message that keeps the typed text. v5 parsed them with parseFloat, so the sweep's synthetic text was saved with a Value of R 0.00; in the app both synthetic entries are refused and the register stays empty (S-timesheet_tab-3).

entries.reason: v5's CSV export writes free-text fields unprotected, so a cell starting with a formula character can run as a formula in a spreadsheet. ClearCase passes every exported user cell through a neutraliser that prefixes such cells, and formula segments after a separator, with an apostrophe. The exception is a validated amount in a signed-money field (Disbursements Amount): it is written as a plain two-decimal number, credits included, with R and grouping removed, where v5 writes what the user typed. Evidence: tests/registers/logic.test.ts:99.
entries.author: GRS-67 dispositions (scripts/verify/register-dispositions.mjs)

entries.reason: v5 exports only the stored fields, so the derived Value is missing from the CSV. ClearCase writes the same stored field keys and rows and does not add the Value column; an app change is needed to export it. Evidence: src/lib/views/registers/logic.ts:90.
entries.author: GRS-67 dispositions (scripts/verify/register-dispositions.mjs)

entries.reason: v5 has no edit, keeps the category after Add and deletes without asking. ClearCase adds a per-row Edit and deletes by stable row id only once confirmed: Delete shows Confirm delete and Cancel inline, and the server deletes nothing unless the request names the confirmed row. The same question also appears on Cross-examination and the other six generic registers. One of the three parts remains: the category still stays after Add. Closing it would need an app change. Evidence: src/lib/views/registers/page.server.ts:133.
entries.author: GRS-67 dispositions (scripts/verify/register-dispositions.mjs)

entries.reason: v5 counts days from local midnight, so counts can differ from the court calendar date near a clock change or in another timezone. ClearCase counts calendar days from today's date in South Africa (Africa/Johannesburg, the court's calendar, UTC+2 all year) to the deadline's date, so the countdown and the Overview's open deadlines no longer depend on the host's time zone. On a host in South Africa they equal v5's. Evidence: tests/registers/deadline-calendar.test.ts:17.
entries.author: GRS-67 dispositions (scripts/verify/register-dispositions.mjs)

entries.reason: v5 keeps large transcript bodies in browser storage with a quota near 5 MB and only alerts on failure. ClearCase stores them in the local case store with a 64 KiB entry limit and shows a failed save with the input kept. Bodies are still rendered whole, the other half of the defect; paging them would need an app change. Evidence: tests/registers/store.test.ts:151.
